Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

suspect verb

think likely; mistrust

also suspicion, suspicious, have a suspicion, I suspect that, suspect someone, arouse suspicion, come under suspicion

classical

Plaut. Men. 5.2.24: id est, quod suspicābar (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Clu. 27: nihil malī suspicāns

suspicor, suspicārī, suspicātus sum

verb, first conjugation, deponent: most often with accusative and infinitive

Usually with accusative and infinitive, of guessing that something is so (suspicor eum domī esse). With a person as object it is rare: of suspecting someone Latin says suspectum habēre (see the suspect).

Other words

  • suspīciō, suspīciōnis f. — suspicion

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 13.10.3: in quem … ulla caderet suspīciō (Lewis & Short); Cic. Verr. 2.5.15: in suspīciōnem venīre; Traupman 158

    With long ī, unlike the verb suspiciō, to look up. Suspīciō cadit in aliquem, suspicion falls on someone; in suspīciōnem venīre, to come under suspicion.

  • suspīciōsus, suspīciōsa, suspīciōsum — suspicious, mistrustful

    also used · classical · Ter. Ad. 4.3.15 (Lewis & Short); Cic. Verr. 2.5.74; Traupman 316

    Ready to suspect, mistrustful, of a person (Ter. Ad. 4.3.15; Cic. Verr. 2.5.74); of a thing that arouses suspicion, suspectus (see the suspect).

  • suspicāx, suspicācis — suspicious, distrustful

    also used · classical · Nep. Timoth. 3.5 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 158

    Lewis & Short: very rare.

  • in suspīciōnem venīre — to come under suspicion

    also used · classical · Nep. Hann. 7 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 158

    With the dative of the person who suspects: in suspīciōnem alicui venīre.

  • suspīciōnem movēre — arouse suspicion

    also used · classical · Cic. Part. Or. 114: quae quidem vel maximē suspīciōnem movent (Lewis & Short s.v. maximē); Traupman 273

  • suspiciō, suspicere, suspexī, suspectum — suspect, mistrust (properly, look up at)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 388

Examples

  • aliquandō dormīsse mē sciō, aliquandō suspicor

    sometimes I know I’ve slept, sometimes I suspect itSen. Ep. 83.6

  • id est, quod suspicābar

    that’s what I suspectedPlaut. Men. 5.2.24 (Lewis & Short)

See also suspect, guess, doubt.
